title: Running Median of a Data Stream
hints: re-sorting from scratch after every insertion is wasteful - you only need access to the middle value(s), not a full ordering
split the numbers into two halves: a 'lower half' holding the smaller values and an 'upper half' holding the larger values, kept the same size (or off by one)
use a max-heap for the lower half (so its largest value, the top, is instantly available) and a min-heap for the upper half (so its smallest value is instantly available)

on each insertion, add the new value to the appropriate heap based on comparison with the lower half's max, then rebalance so the heap sizes differ by at most one. the doubled median is either 2x the larger heap's top (if sizes are unequal) or the sum of both heaps' tops (if sizes are equal)
commonMistakes: letting the two heaps drift out of balance by more than one element, which breaks the median calculation
inserting a new value into the wrong heap without first comparing it against the lower half's current maximum
computing the true fractional median and then flooring or rounding it instead of returning the exact doubled integer sum

content.problemStatement:
Numbers arrive one at a time, given as a list `nums` in arrival order.
After each number is inserted, you need the median of all numbers seen
so far (the middle value when sorted; for an even count, the average of
the two middle values). Since a median can be a fractional value like
1.5, and our numbers must stay integers, return double the median
instead. This is always a whole number, because for an odd count it's
2 times the single middle value, and for an even count it's the sum of
the two middle values (which equals 2 times their average).

**Return an array where the ith entry is 2x the median after the first i+1 numbers have been inserted.**
constraints: the returned array has exactly nums.length elements, one for each running median
notes: a strictly increasing or strictly decreasing stream
negative numbers mixed with positive ones

optimal.time: O(n log n), O(log n) per insertion
optimal.pattern: two heaps - a max-heap for the lower half of values and a min-heap for the upper half, kept balanced in size

bruteForce.approach: after each insertion, sort every number seen so far and compute the median directly from the sorted list
bruteForce.time: O(n^2 log n) across all insertions
